key_claim: Heat pumps move heat instead of making it, so they deliver two to four units of heat per unit of electricity.

slides.headline: A heat pump doesn't make heat. It moves it.
Heat flows downhill, unless you pump it
slides.body: Heat always flows from warm to cold. A heat pump pushes it the other way, like a pump pushing water uphill.

slides.headline: One loop, four steps
slides.body: A liquid soaks up heat as it boils, then gives it off as it turns back to liquid.

slides.headline: Up to four times the heat
slides.body: Moving heat takes less energy than making it. A heat pump gives two to four units of heat for each unit of electricity.

caption:
A heat pump doesn't make heat. It moves it.

1. Heat flows from warm to cold, unless you pump it.
2. A liquid soaks up heat as it boils and gives it off as it condenses.
3. Moving heat takes less energy, so you get 2 to 4 units of heat per unit of electricity.

Source: Waypoint — How Heat Pumps Work
